study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Pinaya et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2019
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Using deep autoencoders to identify abnormal brain structural patterns in neuropsychiatric disorders: A large-scale multi-sample study

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Three public datasets were used: (1) HCP - Human Connectome Project, S1200 Release (March 2017), 1,113 healthy controls used to train the normative deep autoencoder; (2) NUSDAST - Northwestern University Schizophrenia Data and Software Tool, obtained via SchizoConnect, containing healthy controls and schizophrenia patients; (3) ABIDE-I - Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I, containing healthy controls and autism spectrum disorder patients. Only subjects within the HCP age range (22-37 years) were selected from NUSDAST and ABIDE-I.

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The HCP dataset provided the healthy reference population for building the normative model. The deep autoencoder was trained on all 1,113 HCP subjects. The 10-fold cross-validation on HCP was only used for selecting the optimal network architecture (number of neurons per layer), after which the final model was retrained on the whole HCP dataset. The NUSDAST and ABIDE-I datasets served as independent clinical test sets for evaluating the normative model's ability to detect neuroanatomical deviations in patients with schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorder, respectively.

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was built using all 1,113 healthy controls from the HCP dataset. The 10-fold cross-validation on HCP data was performed only to select the optimal network configuration (number of neurons per hidden layer). After determining the best configuration (100-75-100), the model was retrained on the entire HCP dataset (all 1,113 subjects). There was no held-out test set from HCP for the final model; the overall-phase and train-phase are identical.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Since all 1,113 HCP subjects were used for the final normative model training (overall-phase = train-phase), the age statistics are identical for both phases. Mean and SD are directly reported in Table 1. Age range is explicitly stated as 22-37 years. Median and IQR are not reported.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Since all 1,113 HCP subjects were used for the final normative model training (overall-phase = train-phase), the sex statistics are identical for both phases. The paper reports Men=493 (44%) and Women=606 (56%) in Table 1. Note: 493+606=1,099, which does not sum to the stated N=1,113 (discrepancy of 14 subjects). Recalculated percentages: 493/1113=44.3%, 606/1113=54.4%. The discrepancy may be due to 14 subjects with unreported sex data, or rounding/typographical issues in the original paper.
